findings.title: Plugin request logs no longer include traceID
findings.body: The previous implementation explicitly appended the tracing ID from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to every "Plugin Request Completed" log. This diff removes that block, and the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, optional datasource fields, and `uname` to the context attributes. Unless another layer injects traceID, plugin request completion logs lose the field needed to correlate logs with traces.

findings.title: New contextual logger middleware is untested
findings.body: The only test change in this PR is updating the metrics middleware constructor call. There is no test that verifies the newly extracted `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` actually enriches the context with `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `uname`, nor that `LoggerMiddleware` now emits those contextual fields via `FromContext`. A regression where context attributes are dropped or not propagated would pass CI.

findings.title: FromContext silently discards context when the concrete type assertion fails
findings.body: `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` returns the infrastructure `log.Logger` interface, but the wrapper asserts it to `*log.ConcreteLogger` and falls back to `d.New()` if that assertion fails. If the infrastructure logger returns a context-aware wrapper or any other implementation, the fallback returns a logger without the supplied context, silently dropping all contextual fields. Since `LoggerMiddleware` now relies on this method for plugin request fields, that failure mode would make contextual logging appear enabled while losing the data.
